_comment: 報連相：連絡 の 講義ページ 5節「人に よって、好きな 方法が ちがう」の 絵（2026-10-30）。報連相の 絵に 出るのは 藤木取締役・ヘンディ・奥田さん・富田さん・ニャムの 5人だけ（注意事項 2026-08-30）なので、電話が 好きな 人を ヘンディ、チャットが 好きな 人を 奥田さんに した（1回目は 人物カードの ない 2人で 描いて いた）。参照の 1枚目は s1（絵柄と 若手エンジニア）、2枚目・3枚目が 設定画。吹き出しは 1行で 書かせる（2行に 折ると 2行目の 漢字の ふりがなが 抜けた）。
style: Warm modern anime illustration, like a friendly Japanese educational manga — clean confident black linework, flat cel shading with gentle light, bright natural daylight, soft pastel palette of sky blue, cream and coral, rounded friendly shapes. A tidy contemporary Japanese software office with real desks, chairs, windows, plants, mugs and laptops. People are drawn as real human beings with natural proportions, warm friendly faces and exactly five fingers on each hand, no tangled or merged fingers. Match the drawing style and the colours of the FIRST reference picture exactly. Three different people appear and they must never look alike. THE JUNIOR ENGINEER is the young man of the FIRST reference picture with short dark brown hair wearing a coral-orange shirt jacket over a white tee, no glasses. HENDY is the man in the SECOND reference picture (his character sheet): short black hair, a navy suit, white shirt and navy tie, no glasses. OKUDA is the man in the THIRD reference picture (his character sheet): wavy messy black hair, black rectangular thick-rimmed glasses, a dark green pullover hoodie. Only Okuda wears glasses and a green hoodie; only Hendy wears a suit and tie. This is a TEACHING picture, not a mood picture: a student who can hardly read Japanese must understand the message from the picture alone. EMOTIONS ARE BIG AND OBVIOUS, like a Japanese comedy manga — exaggerated faces and whole-body poses that read from across the room. Happy and relieved people beam with huge open smiles and sparkling eyes, raise a fist or give a thumbs-up, with little sparkles around them. Puzzled people tilt their heads under a big question mark. Manga symbols are welcome and carry the message: big question marks, exclamation marks, sweat drops, lightbulbs, sparkles, motion lines, check marks.
noText: Lettering — read this part carefully. The picture contains ONLY the words listed above, and no other writing at all. Print each Japanese word LARGE and horizontally in a bold rounded gothic Japanese font, with generous space around it — either on a soft cream label with a rounded border, or inside a white speech balloon whose tail clearly points at the person who says it. Directly above every kanji, print its reading in small hiragana (furigana), centred over that kanji, clearly separated from it, at about 45% of the kanji height, so that the kanji and the furigana both stay sharp. Words written only in hiragana or katakana take no furigana, and Latin letters and numbers take no furigana either. The readings in round brackets are for you only — never print the brackets or the reading in the brackets as text. Spell every character exactly as given. Screens, papers and whiteboards show only soft abstract shapes apart from the listed words. No other letters, numbers, logos or watermarks anywhere in the picture.
negative: Never: photo-realistic rendering, harsh shadows, extra or merged fingers, distorted hands, horror or a scary dark mood, real grief, violence, watermarks, real company logos or brand marks of any kind (no fruit logo on laptops or phones, no chat-app logos), national flags, country outlines, maps with borders, tiny cluttered text, paragraphs of text, 3D render, flat vector icon art, pictograms floating on an empty background, robots, mascots.

scenes.scene: THE ONE IDEA THIS PICTURE MUST MAKE OBVIOUS: one colleague likes phone calls, another likes chat, so you look at the person and choose. A wide medium shot in the bright office, on a soft cream ground. At the top centre sits one wide rounded cream label panel carrying the first word below. LEFT: HENDY stands by his desk holding up his smartphone towards the viewer with a huge open grin and sparkles, and a white speech balloon from him says the second word below. RIGHT: OKUDA sits at his laptop with headphones around his neck; behind him a wall calendar is packed with coloured meeting blocks; he smiles and points with one hand at his laptop screen, which shows a chat window of soft grey abstract bubbles, and a white speech balloon from him says the third word below. CENTRE FRONT: the junior engineer stands between them, looking from one to the other with wide, attentive eyes; two thin dotted sight lines run from his eyes to each colleague, and a big glowing lightbulb shines above his head, showing that he has noticed what each person likes. Warm daylight, plants, mugs. LETTERING LAYOUT — this matters as much as the people: each speech balloon is wide and holds its words on ONE single horizontal line, never broken into two lines, so that every kanji has clear room above it for its furigana. EVERY kanji in this picture carries its furigana — 人 in the label panel, BOTH kanji of 電話 and the 話 of 話そう in Hendy's balloon, and the 願 of お願い in Okuda's balloon. No kanji is left without its reading.
text: 人に よって ちがう（ひとに よって ちがう）
電話で 話そう！（でんわで はなそう！）
チャットで お願い！（チャットで おねがい！）
